name: Josef Fleischmann
current_role: Founder, Bavaria Instruments (in-orbit computing); Co-Founder and shareholder, Isar Aerospace
profile: Aerospace engineer (Josef Peter Fleischmann) who co-founded Isar Aerospace in 2018 with Daniel Metzler and Markus Brandl out of TUM's WARR rocketry group, serving as COO and later CTO and building its in-house manufacturing and test infrastructure in Germany and Sweden. After Spectrum reached orbit in Sept 2026 he handed over operations to found Bavaria Instruments, keeping his Isar stake.
interesting_fact: Weeks after Isar's Spectrum became the first commercial rocket from continental Europe to reach orbit (5 Sept 2026), he launched Bavaria Instruments to build in-orbit computing for real-time Earth observation and autonomous spacecraft.
deep_cut_fact: Back in Dec 2021, as Isar's COO when the company had ~220 staff, he gave a Forbes DACH Under 30 Summit talk titled 'The 21st Century Space Race'. Isar chairman Bulent Altan (ex-SpaceX) has described him as someone who builds 'what others are just blueprinting'.
notes: Newly launched Bavaria Instruments (Sept 2026) means he is likely open to press; the Bavaria Instruments press email is the best route. Bavaria Instruments website did not load during research. Web-search budget ran out during this lane, so the deep-cut fact rests on a Wikipedia-cited YouTube talk listing plus the Isar press release.

name: David Crawshaw
current_role: Founder, exe.dev (cloud/VM platform, funding announced April 2026); Co-Founder, Tailscale
profile: Software engineer who spent years at Google working on the Go language (incl. mobile/cgo work) and the Fuchsia OS, left in 2018, and co-founded Tailscale in 2019 with Avery Pennarun, David Carney and Brad Fitzpatrick (last priced at ~$1.5B in 2025). In April 2026 he announced funding for a new company, exe.dev, to build a cloud that is 'just good Linux VMs' done right.
interesting_fact: Explaining why he started exe.dev while Tailscale was thriving, he wrote simply: 'I like computers... So it is no small thing for me when I admit: I do not like the cloud today.'
deep_cut_fact: In a 2016 blog post, 'Limits of Superintelligence', he argued that with Moore's law ending, machine intelligence per Joule becomes fixed, so AI progress is 'now tied to... our industrial output' - an early take on AI being bounded by energy and compute buildout.
notes: Self-published email on his own blog. Writes thoughtfully about programming with AI agents (2025-2026 posts) and data-center/cloud economics - highly relevant to a data-center podcast. Not listed among Tailscale's current key people on Wikipedia, so his focus now appears to be exe.dev.

name: Etienne Lacroix
profile: Montreal engineer-entrepreneur who founded Vention in 2016, a cloud platform where manufacturers design, order and deploy modular automation and robot cells (MachineBuilder, MachineMotion AI). Previously at McKinsey and GE; Vention now serves ~90 Fortune 500 manufacturers and is pushing into 'physical AI', which it says is its fastest-growing segment.
interesting_fact: In Sept 2026 Vention opened a Physical AI lab in Montreal, advised by Cohere's Joelle Pineau, training robotic manipulation on data from its install base; physical-AI revenue grew ~400% in a year.
deep_cut_fact: Before Vention he developed industrial technologies at GE and advised manufacturers from aerospace to consumer electronics at McKinsey; he trained as a mechanical engineer at Montreal's École de technologie supérieure (ÉTS) before his Harvard MBA.
notes: Outspoken on manufacturing policy (Bloomberg Oct 2025 feature on tariffs). No dedicated press email found on the press page; newswire releases were blocked by a bot check. Use info@ or the contact form. Strong fit for an automation/physical-AI episode.
